# FindnetCDF.cmake
#
# Finds the NetCDF-C library using nc-config as a fallback when
# netCDFConfig.cmake is not available (common with Autotools/HPC installs).
#
# Sets:
#   netCDF_FOUND        - TRUE if NetCDF-C was found
#   netCDF_INCLUDE_DIRS - Include directories
#   netCDF_LIBRARIES    - Libraries to link
#   netCDF_VERSION      - Version string
#
# Creates imported target:
#   netCDF::netcdf      - The NetCDF-C library

if(netCDF_FOUND)
  return()
endif()

# Step 1: Try to find nc-config
find_program(NETCDF_NC_CONFIG nc-config
  HINTS ENV NETCDF_DIR ENV NETCDF_ROOT
  PATH_SUFFIXES bin
)

if(NETCDF_NC_CONFIG)
  # Query nc-config for installation details
  execute_process(
    COMMAND ${NETCDF_NC_CONFIG} --prefix
    OUTPUT_VARIABLE NETCDF_PREFIX
    OUTPUT_STRIP_TRAILING_WHITESPACE
    ERROR_QUIET
  )
  execute_process(
    COMMAND ${NETCDF_NC_CONFIG} --includedir
    OUTPUT_VARIABLE NETCDF_INCLUDE_DIR
    OUTPUT_STRIP_TRAILING_WHITESPACE
    ERROR_QUIET
  )
  execute_process(
    COMMAND ${NETCDF_NC_CONFIG} --libdir
    OUTPUT_VARIABLE NETCDF_LIB_DIR
    OUTPUT_STRIP_TRAILING_WHITESPACE
    ERROR_QUIET
  )
  execute_process(
    COMMAND ${NETCDF_NC_CONFIG} --version
    OUTPUT_VARIABLE NETCDF_VERSION_RAW
    OUTPUT_STRIP_TRAILING_WHITESPACE
    ERROR_QUIET
  )

  # Parse version: "netCDF 4.9.3" -> "4.9.3"
  if(NETCDF_VERSION_RAW)
    string(REGEX REPLACE "^netCDF[ \t]+" "" netCDF_VERSION "${NETCDF_VERSION_RAW}")
  endif()

  # Find the actual library file
  find_library(netCDF_LIBRARY
    NAMES netcdf
    HINTS ${NETCDF_LIB_DIR} ${NETCDF_PREFIX}/lib
  )

  set(netCDF_INCLUDE_DIRS ${NETCDF_INCLUDE_DIR})
  set(netCDF_LIBRARIES ${netCDF_LIBRARY})

else()
  # Step 2: Fall back to manual search in standard paths
  find_path(NETCDF_INCLUDE_DIR
    NAMES netcdf.h
    HINTS ENV NETCDF_DIR ENV NETCDF_ROOT
    PATH_SUFFIXES include
  )
  find_library(netCDF_LIBRARY
    NAMES netcdf
    HINTS ENV NETCDF_DIR ENV NETCDF_ROOT
    PATH_SUFFIXES lib lib64
  )

  set(netCDF_INCLUDE_DIRS ${NETCDF_INCLUDE_DIR})
  set(netCDF_LIBRARIES ${netCDF_LIBRARY})
endif()

# Standard CMake find_package handling
include(FindPackageHandleStandardArgs)
find_package_handle_standard_args(netCDF
  REQUIRED_VARS netCDF_LIBRARIES netCDF_INCLUDE_DIRS
  VERSION_VAR netCDF_VERSION
)

# Create imported target if found
if(netCDF_FOUND AND NOT TARGET netCDF::netcdf)
  add_library(netCDF::netcdf UNKNOWN IMPORTED)
  set_target_properties(netCDF::netcdf PROPERTIES
    IMPORTED_LOCATION "${netCDF_LIBRARY}"
    INTERFACE_INCLUDE_DIRECTORIES "${netCDF_INCLUDE_DIRS}"
  )
endif()

mark_as_advanced(NETCDF_NC_CONFIG netCDF_LIBRARY NETCDF_INCLUDE_DIR)

module miem_mod
  use iso_c_binding
  use miem_util_mod
  use miem_emis_state_mod
  implicit none
  private

  type, public :: miem_t
    type(c_ptr), private :: ptr = c_null_ptr
    integer :: n_cells = 0
    integer :: n_vert_levels = 0
  contains
    procedure :: init => miem_init
    procedure :: run => miem_run
    procedure :: resolve_host_indices => miem_resolve_host_indices
    procedure :: num_species => miem_num_species
    procedure :: finalize => miem_finalize
  end type miem_t

  public :: miem_query_species_count

  ! C function interfaces
  interface
    function CreateMIEM_c(config_path, n_cells, n_vert_levels, error) &
        bind(C, name="CreateMIEM")
      import :: c_ptr, c_char, c_int
      character(kind=c_char), intent(in) :: config_path(*)
      integer(c_int), value :: n_cells
      integer(c_int), value :: n_vert_levels
      type(c_ptr), value :: error
      type(c_ptr) :: CreateMIEM_c
    end function

    subroutine DeleteMIEM_c(miem, error) bind(C, name="DeleteMIEM")
      import :: c_ptr
      type(c_ptr), value :: miem
      type(c_ptr), value :: error
    end subroutine

    function MIEMRun_c(miem, time, dt, air_density, layer_thickness, &
        n_atm_elements, error) bind(C, name="MIEMRun")
      import :: c_ptr, c_double, c_int
      type(c_ptr), value :: miem
      real(c_double), value :: time
      real(c_double), value :: dt
      type(c_ptr), value :: air_density
      type(c_ptr), value :: layer_thickness
      integer(c_int), value :: n_atm_elements
      type(c_ptr), value :: error
      type(c_ptr) :: MIEMRun_c
    end function

    subroutine MIEMResolveHostIndices_c(miem, host_names, n_host, indices, error) &
        bind(C, name="MIEMResolveHostIndices")
      import :: c_ptr, c_int
      type(c_ptr), value :: miem
      type(c_ptr), value :: host_names
      integer(c_int), value :: n_host
      type(c_ptr), value :: indices
      type(c_ptr), value :: error
    end subroutine

    function MIEMGetNumSpecies_c(miem) bind(C, name="MIEMGetNumSpecies")
      import :: c_ptr, c_int
      type(c_ptr), value :: miem
      integer(c_int) :: MIEMGetNumSpecies_c
    end function

    function MIEMQuerySpeciesCount_c(config_path, error) &
        bind(C, name="MIEMQuerySpeciesCount")
      import :: c_ptr, c_char, c_int
      character(kind=c_char), intent(in) :: config_path(*)
      type(c_ptr), value :: error
      integer(c_int) :: MIEMQuerySpeciesCount_c
    end function

    subroutine MIEMQuerySpeciesNames_c(config_path, names, max_names, error) &
        bind(C, name="MIEMQuerySpeciesNames")
      import :: c_ptr, c_char, c_int
      character(kind=c_char), intent(in) :: config_path(*)
      type(c_ptr), value :: names
      integer(c_int), value :: max_names
      type(c_ptr), value :: error
    end subroutine
  end interface

contains

  subroutine miem_init(this, config_path, n_cells, n_vert_levels, error)
    class(miem_t), intent(inout) :: this
    character(len=*), intent(in) :: config_path
    integer, intent(in) :: n_cells
    integer, intent(in) :: n_vert_levels
    type(error_t), intent(inout), target :: error

    character(len=len_trim(config_path)+1, kind=c_char) :: c_config

    c_config = f_to_c_string(config_path)
    this%ptr = CreateMIEM_c(c_config, int(n_cells, c_int), &
                            int(n_vert_levels, c_int), c_loc(error))
    this%n_cells = n_cells
    this%n_vert_levels = n_vert_levels
  end subroutine

  subroutine miem_run(this, time_current, dt, air_density, layer_thickness, &
                      state, error)
    class(miem_t), intent(inout) :: this
    real(c_double), intent(in) :: time_current
    real(c_double), intent(in) :: dt
    real(c_double), intent(in), target :: air_density(:)
    real(c_double), intent(in), target :: layer_thickness(:)
    type(emis_state_t), intent(out) :: state
    type(error_t), intent(inout), target :: error

    integer(c_int) :: n_atm

    type(c_ptr) :: state_ptr

    n_atm = int(size(air_density), c_int)
    state_ptr = MIEMRun_c(this%ptr, time_current, dt, &
                           c_loc(air_density(1)), c_loc(layer_thickness(1)), &
                           n_atm, c_loc(error))
    call state%set_ptr(state_ptr)

    if (error_is_success(error) .and. state%is_associated()) then
      call state%update_references()
    end if
  end subroutine

  subroutine miem_resolve_host_indices(this, host_species, indices, error)
    class(miem_t), intent(inout) :: this
    character(len=*), intent(in) :: host_species(:)
    integer(c_int), intent(out), target :: indices(:)
    type(error_t), intent(inout), target :: error

    type(c_ptr), allocatable, target :: c_names(:)
    character(len=64, kind=c_char), allocatable, target :: c_strings(:)
    integer :: i, n

    n = size(host_species)
    allocate(c_names(n))
    allocate(c_strings(n))

    do i = 1, n
      c_strings(i) = f_to_c_string(host_species(i))
      c_names(i) = c_loc(c_strings(i))
    end do

    call MIEMResolveHostIndices_c(this%ptr, c_loc(c_names(1)), &
                                  int(n, c_int), c_loc(indices(1)), c_loc(error))
  end subroutine

  function miem_num_species(this) result(n)
    class(miem_t), intent(in) :: this
    integer :: n
    n = MIEMGetNumSpecies_c(this%ptr)
  end function

  function miem_query_species_count(config_path, error) result(n)
    character(len=*), intent(in) :: config_path
    type(error_t), intent(inout), target :: error
    integer :: n

    character(len=len_trim(config_path)+1, kind=c_char) :: c_config

    c_config = f_to_c_string(config_path)
    n = MIEMQuerySpeciesCount_c(c_config, c_loc(error))
  end function

  subroutine miem_finalize(this, error)
    class(miem_t), intent(inout) :: this
    type(error_t), intent(inout), target :: error

    if (c_associated(this%ptr)) then
      call DeleteMIEM_c(this%ptr, c_loc(error))
      this%ptr = c_null_ptr
    end if
  end subroutine

end module miem_mod

module miem_emis_state_mod
  use iso_c_binding
  use miem_util_mod
  implicit none
  private

  type, public :: emis_state_t
    type(c_ptr), private :: ptr = c_null_ptr
    integer :: n_species = 0
    integer :: n_cells = 0
    integer :: n_vert_levels = 0
    real(c_double), pointer :: surface_flux(:,:) => null()
    real(c_double), pointer :: tendency(:,:,:) => null()
    integer(c_int), pointer :: emis_to_chem_idx(:) => null()
  contains
    procedure :: update_references => emis_state_update_references
    procedure :: delete => emis_state_delete
    procedure :: set_ptr => emis_state_set_ptr
    procedure :: is_associated => emis_state_is_associated
  end type emis_state_t

  ! C function interfaces
  interface
    function MIEMGetSurfaceFlux_c(state) bind(C, name="MIEMGetSurfaceFlux")
      import :: c_ptr
      type(c_ptr), value :: state
      type(c_ptr) :: MIEMGetSurfaceFlux_c
    end function

    function MIEMGetTendency_c(state) bind(C, name="MIEMGetTendency")
      import :: c_ptr
      type(c_ptr), value :: state
      type(c_ptr) :: MIEMGetTendency_c
    end function

    function MIEMGetEmisToChemIdx_c(state) bind(C, name="MIEMGetEmisToChemIdx")
      import :: c_ptr
      type(c_ptr), value :: state
      type(c_ptr) :: MIEMGetEmisToChemIdx_c
    end function

    function MIEMGetStateNumSpecies_c(state) bind(C, name="MIEMGetStateNumSpecies")
      import :: c_ptr, c_int
      type(c_ptr), value :: state
      integer(c_int) :: MIEMGetStateNumSpecies_c
    end function

    function MIEMGetStateNumCells_c(state) bind(C, name="MIEMGetStateNumCells")
      import :: c_ptr, c_int
      type(c_ptr), value :: state
      integer(c_int) :: MIEMGetStateNumCells_c
    end function

    function MIEMGetStateNumVertLevels_c(state) bind(C, name="MIEMGetStateNumVertLevels")
      import :: c_ptr, c_int
      type(c_ptr), value :: state
      integer(c_int) :: MIEMGetStateNumVertLevels_c
    end function

    subroutine DeleteMIEMState_c(state, error) bind(C, name="DeleteMIEMState")
      import :: c_ptr
      type(c_ptr), value :: state
      type(c_ptr), value :: error
    end subroutine
  end interface

contains

  subroutine emis_state_update_references(this)
    class(emis_state_t), intent(inout) :: this
    type(c_ptr) :: data_ptr

    if (.not. c_associated(this%ptr)) return

    this%n_species = MIEMGetStateNumSpecies_c(this%ptr)
    this%n_cells = MIEMGetStateNumCells_c(this%ptr)
    this%n_vert_levels = MIEMGetStateNumVertLevels_c(this%ptr)

    ! Surface flux: (n_species, n_cells) — species-major in C, becomes (n_cells, n_species)
    data_ptr = MIEMGetSurfaceFlux_c(this%ptr)
    if (c_associated(data_ptr) .and. this%n_species > 0 .and. this%n_cells > 0) then
      call c_f_pointer(data_ptr, this%surface_flux, [this%n_cells, this%n_species])
    end if

    ! Tendency: (n_species * n_vert_levels, n_cells)
    data_ptr = MIEMGetTendency_c(this%ptr)
    if (c_associated(data_ptr) .and. this%n_species > 0 .and. this%n_cells > 0 &
        .and. this%n_vert_levels > 0) then
      call c_f_pointer(data_ptr, this%tendency, &
          [this%n_cells, this%n_vert_levels, this%n_species])
    end if

    ! Emissions-to-chemistry index mapping
    data_ptr = MIEMGetEmisToChemIdx_c(this%ptr)
    if (c_associated(data_ptr) .and. this%n_species > 0) then
      call c_f_pointer(data_ptr, this%emis_to_chem_idx, [this%n_species])
    end if
  end subroutine

  subroutine emis_state_delete(this, error)
    class(emis_state_t), intent(inout) :: this
    type(error_t), intent(inout), target :: error

    if (c_associated(this%ptr)) then
      call DeleteMIEMState_c(this%ptr, c_loc(error))
      this%ptr = c_null_ptr
    end if

    this%surface_flux => null()
    this%tendency => null()
    this%emis_to_chem_idx => null()
    this%n_species = 0
    this%n_cells = 0
    this%n_vert_levels = 0
  end subroutine

  subroutine emis_state_set_ptr(this, new_ptr)
    class(emis_state_t), intent(inout) :: this
    type(c_ptr), intent(in) :: new_ptr
    this%ptr = new_ptr
  end subroutine

  function emis_state_is_associated(this) result(assoc)
    class(emis_state_t), intent(in) :: this
    logical :: assoc
    assoc = c_associated(this%ptr)
  end function

end module miem_emis_state_mod

module miem_util_mod
  use iso_c_binding
  implicit none

  ! Error type matching C MIEMError struct
  type, bind(C) :: error_t
    integer(c_int) :: code = 0
    character(kind=c_char) :: category(64)
    character(kind=c_char) :: message(256)
  end type error_t

  interface
    ! String helper: convert C char array to Fortran string
  end interface

contains

  function error_is_success(error) result(success)
    type(error_t), intent(in) :: error
    logical :: success
    success = (error%code == 0)
  end function

  function error_message(error) result(msg)
    type(error_t), intent(in) :: error
    character(len=255) :: msg
    integer :: i

    msg = ' '
    do i = 1, 255
      if (error%message(i) == c_null_char) exit
      msg(i:i) = error%message(i)
    end do
  end function

  function error_category(error) result(cat)
    type(error_t), intent(in) :: error
    character(len=63) :: cat
    integer :: i

    cat = ' '
    do i = 1, 63
      if (error%category(i) == c_null_char) exit
      cat(i:i) = error%category(i)
    end do
  end function

  ! Convert a Fortran string to a null-terminated C string
  function f_to_c_string(f_str) result(c_str)
    character(len=*), intent(in) :: f_str
    character(len=len_trim(f_str)+1, kind=c_char) :: c_str

    c_str = trim(f_str) // c_null_char
  end function

end module miem_util_mod

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
**Phase 1 (build system)** is the foundation — everything else depends on clean linking and correct dependency visibility. The `PUBLIC` vs `PRIVATE` fix alone prevents yaml-cpp and NetCDF from contaminating downstream build graphs. The NetCDF target name aliasing is a subtle but common pitfall: CMake config-mode packages and Find modules often create targets with slightly different names.

# FindnetCDF.cmake
#
# Finds the NetCDF-C library using nc-config as a fallback when
# netCDFConfig.cmake is not available (common with Autotools/HPC installs).
#
# Sets:
#   netCDF_FOUND        - TRUE if NetCDF-C was found
#   netCDF_INCLUDE_DIRS - Include directories
#   netCDF_LIBRARIES    - Libraries to link
#   netCDF_VERSION      - Version string
#
# Creates imported target:
#   netCDF::netcdf      - The NetCDF-C library

if(netCDF_FOUND)
  return()
endif()

# Step 1: Try to find nc-config
find_program(NETCDF_NC_CONFIG nc-config
  HINTS ENV NETCDF_DIR ENV NETCDF_ROOT
  PATH_SUFFIXES bin
)

if(NETCDF_NC_CONFIG)
  # Query nc-config for installation details
  execute_process(
    COMMAND ${NETCDF_NC_CONFIG} --prefix
    OUTPUT_VARIABLE NETCDF_PREFIX
    OUTPUT_STRIP_TRAILING_WHITESPACE
    ERROR_QUIET
  )
  execute_process(
    COMMAND ${NETCDF_NC_CONFIG} --includedir
    OUTPUT_VARIABLE NETCDF_INCLUDE_DIR
    OUTPUT_STRIP_TRAILING_WHITESPACE
    ERROR_QUIET
  )
  execute_process(
    COMMAND ${NETCDF_NC_CONFIG} --libdir
    OUTPUT_VARIABLE NETCDF_LIB_DIR
    OUTPUT_STRIP_TRAILING_WHITESPACE
    ERROR_QUIET
  )
  execute_process(
    COMMAND ${NETCDF_NC_CONFIG} --version
    OUTPUT_VARIABLE NETCDF_VERSION_RAW
    OUTPUT_STRIP_TRAILING_WHITESPACE
    ERROR_QUIET
  )

  # Parse version: "netCDF 4.9.3" -> "4.9.3"
  if(NETCDF_VERSION_RAW)
    string(REGEX REPLACE "^netCDF[ \t]+" "" netCDF_VERSION "${NETCDF_VERSION_RAW}")
  endif()

  # Find the actual library file
  find_library(netCDF_LIBRARY
    NAMES netcdf
    HINTS ${NETCDF_LIB_DIR} ${NETCDF_PREFIX}/lib
  )

  set(netCDF_INCLUDE_DIRS ${NETCDF_INCLUDE_DIR})
  set(netCDF_LIBRARIES ${netCDF_LIBRARY})

else()
  # Step 2: Fall back to manual search in standard paths
  find_path(NETCDF_INCLUDE_DIR
    NAMES netcdf.h
    HINTS ENV NETCDF_DIR ENV NETCDF_ROOT
    PATH_SUFFIXES include
  )
  find_library(netCDF_LIBRARY
    NAMES netcdf
    HINTS ENV NETCDF_DIR ENV NETCDF_ROOT
    PATH_SUFFIXES lib lib64
  )

  set(netCDF_INCLUDE_DIRS ${NETCDF_INCLUDE_DIR})
  set(netCDF_LIBRARIES ${netCDF_LIBRARY})
endif()

# Standard CMake find_package handling
include(FindPackageHandleStandardArgs)
find_package_handle_standard_args(netCDF
  REQUIRED_VARS netCDF_LIBRARIES netCDF_INCLUDE_DIRS
  VERSION_VAR netCDF_VERSION
)

# Create imported target if found
if(netCDF_FOUND AND NOT TARGET netCDF::netcdf)
  add_library(netCDF::netcdf UNKNOWN IMPORTED)
  set_target_properties(netCDF::netcdf PROPERTIES
    IMPORTED_LOCATION "${netCDF_LIBRARY}"
    INTERFACE_INCLUDE_DIRECTORIES "${netCDF_INCLUDE_DIRS}"
  )
endif()

mark_as_advanced(NETCDF_NC_CONFIG netCDF_LIBRARY NETCDF_INCLUDE_DIR)

module miem_emis_state_mod
  use iso_c_binding
  use miem_util_mod
  implicit none
  private

  type, public :: emis_state_t
    type(c_ptr), private :: ptr = c_null_ptr
    integer :: n_species = 0
    integer :: n_cells = 0
    integer :: n_vert_levels = 0
    real(c_double), pointer :: surface_flux(:,:) => null()
    real(c_double), pointer :: tendency(:,:,:) => null()
    integer(c_int), pointer :: emis_to_chem_idx(:) => null()
  contains
    procedure :: update_references => emis_state_update_references
    procedure :: delete => emis_state_delete
    procedure :: set_ptr => emis_state_set_ptr
    procedure :: is_associated => emis_state_is_associated
  end type emis_state_t

  ! C function interfaces
  interface
    function MIEMGetSurfaceFlux_c(state) bind(C, name="MIEMGetSurfaceFlux")
      import :: c_ptr
      type(c_ptr), value :: state
      type(c_ptr) :: MIEMGetSurfaceFlux_c
    end function

    function MIEMGetTendency_c(state) bind(C, name="MIEMGetTendency")
      import :: c_ptr
      type(c_ptr), value :: state
      type(c_ptr) :: MIEMGetTendency_c
    end function

    function MIEMGetEmisToChemIdx_c(state) bind(C, name="MIEMGetEmisToChemIdx")
      import :: c_ptr
      type(c_ptr), value :: state
      type(c_ptr) :: MIEMGetEmisToChemIdx_c
    end function

    function MIEMGetStateNumSpecies_c(state) bind(C, name="MIEMGetStateNumSpecies")
      import :: c_ptr, c_int
      type(c_ptr), value :: state
      integer(c_int) :: MIEMGetStateNumSpecies_c
    end function

    function MIEMGetStateNumCells_c(state) bind(C, name="MIEMGetStateNumCells")
      import :: c_ptr, c_int
      type(c_ptr), value :: state
      integer(c_int) :: MIEMGetStateNumCells_c
    end function

    function MIEMGetStateNumVertLevels_c(state) bind(C, name="MIEMGetStateNumVertLevels")
      import :: c_ptr, c_int
      type(c_ptr), value :: state
      integer(c_int) :: MIEMGetStateNumVertLevels_c
    end function

    subroutine DeleteMIEMState_c(state, error) bind(C, name="DeleteMIEMState")
      import :: c_ptr
      type(c_ptr), value :: state
      type(c_ptr), value :: error
    end subroutine
  end interface

contains

  subroutine emis_state_update_references(this)
    class(emis_state_t), intent(inout) :: this
    type(c_ptr) :: data_ptr

    if (.not. c_associated(this%ptr)) return

    this%n_species = MIEMGetStateNumSpecies_c(this%ptr)
    this%n_cells = MIEMGetStateNumCells_c(this%ptr)
    this%n_vert_levels = MIEMGetStateNumVertLevels_c(this%ptr)

    ! Surface flux: (n_species, n_cells) — species-major in C, becomes (n_cells, n_species)
    data_ptr = MIEMGetSurfaceFlux_c(this%ptr)
    if (c_associated(data_ptr) .and. this%n_species > 0 .and. this%n_cells > 0) then
      call c_f_pointer(data_ptr, this%surface_flux, [this%n_cells, this%n_species])
    end if

    ! Tendency: (n_species * n_vert_levels, n_cells)
    data_ptr = MIEMGetTendency_c(this%ptr)
    if (c_associated(data_ptr) .and. this%n_species > 0 .and. this%n_cells > 0 &
        .and. this%n_vert_levels > 0) then
      call c_f_pointer(data_ptr, this%tendency, &
          [this%n_cells, this%n_vert_levels, this%n_species])
    end if

    ! Emissions-to-chemistry index mapping
    data_ptr = MIEMGetEmisToChemIdx_c(this%ptr)
    if (c_associated(data_ptr) .and. this%n_species > 0) then
      call c_f_pointer(data_ptr, this%emis_to_chem_idx, [this%n_species])
    end if
  end subroutine

  subroutine emis_state_delete(this, error)
    class(emis_state_t), intent(inout) :: this
    type(error_t), intent(inout), target :: error

    if (c_associated(this%ptr)) then
      call DeleteMIEMState_c(this%ptr, c_loc(error))
      this%ptr = c_null_ptr
    end if

    this%surface_flux => null()
    this%tendency => null()
    this%emis_to_chem_idx => null()
    this%n_species = 0
    this%n_cells = 0
    this%n_vert_levels = 0
  end subroutine

  subroutine emis_state_set_ptr(this, new_ptr)
    class(emis_state_t), intent(inout) :: this
    type(c_ptr), intent(in) :: new_ptr
    this%ptr = new_ptr
  end subroutine

  function emis_state_is_associated(this) result(assoc)
    class(emis_state_t), intent(in) :: this
    logical :: assoc
    assoc = c_associated(this%ptr)
  end function

end module miem_emis_state_mod

    end function

    subroutine DeleteMIEMState_c(state, error) bind(C, name="DeleteMIEMState")
      import :: c_ptr

    end subroutine

  subroutine emis_state_update_references(this)
    class(emis_state_t), intent(inout) :: this
    type(c_ptr) :: data_ptr

    if (.not. c_associated(this%ptr)) return

    this%n_species = MIEMGetStateNumSpecies_c(this%ptr)
    this%n_cells = MIEMGetStateNumCells_c(this%ptr)
    this%n_vert_levels = MIEMGetStateNumVertLevels_c(this%ptr)

    ! Surface flux: (n_species, n_cells) — species-major in C, becomes (n_cells, n_species)
    data_ptr = MIEMGetSurfaceFlux_c(this%ptr)
    if (c_associated(data_ptr) .and. this%n_species > 0 .and. this%n_cells > 0) then
      call c_f_pointer(data_ptr, this%surface_flux, [this%n_cells, this%n_species])
    end if

    ! Tendency: (n_species * n_vert_levels, n_cells)
    data_ptr = MIEMGetTendency_c(this%ptr)
    if (c_associated(data_ptr) .and. this%n_species > 0 .and. this%n_cells > 0 &
        .and. this%n_vert_levels > 0) then
      call c_f_pointer(data_ptr, this%tendency, &
          [this%n_cells, this%n_vert_levels, this%n_species])
    end if

    ! Emissions-to-chemistry index mapping
    data_ptr = MIEMGetEmisToChemIdx_c(this%ptr)
    if (c_associated(data_ptr) .and. this%n_species > 0) then
      call c_f_pointer(data_ptr, this%emis_to_chem_idx, [this%n_species])
    end if
  end subroutine

  subroutine emis_state_delete(this, error)
    class(emis_state_t), intent(inout) :: this
    type(error_t), intent(inout), target :: error

    if (c_associated(this%ptr)) then
      call DeleteMIEMState_c(this%ptr, c_loc(error))
      this%ptr = c_null_ptr
    end if

    this%surface_flux => null()
    this%tendency => null()
    this%emis_to_chem_idx => null()
    this%n_species = 0
    this%n_cells = 0
    this%n_vert_levels = 0
  end subroutine

  subroutine emis_state_set_ptr(this, new_ptr)
    class(emis_state_t), intent(inout) :: this
    type(c_ptr), intent(in) :: new_ptr
    this%ptr = new_ptr
  end subroutine

  function emis_state_is_associated(this) result(assoc)
    class(emis_state_t), intent(in) :: this
    logical :: assoc
    assoc = c_associated(this%ptr)
  end function

module miem_util_mod
  use iso_c_binding
  implicit none

  ! Error type matching C MIEMError struct
  type, bind(C) :: error_t
    integer(c_int) :: code = 0
    character(kind=c_char) :: category(64)

contains

  function error_is_success(error) result(success)
    type(error_t), intent(in) :: error
    logical :: success
    success = (error%code == 0)
  end function

  function error_message(error) result(msg)
    type(error_t), intent(in) :: error
    character(len=255) :: msg
    integer :: i

    msg = ' '
    do i = 1, 255
      if (error%message(i) == c_null_char) exit
      msg(i:i) = error%message(i)
    end do
  end function

  function error_category(error) result(cat)
    type(error_t), intent(in) :: error
    character(len=63) :: cat
    integer :: i

    cat = ' '
    do i = 1, 63
      if (error%category(i) == c_null_char) exit
      cat(i:i) = error%category(i)
    end do
  end function

  ! Convert a Fortran string to a null-terminated C string
  function f_to_c_string(f_str) result(c_str)
    character(len=*), intent(in) :: f_str
    character(len=len_trim(f_str)+1, kind=c_char) :: c_str

    c_str = trim(f_str) // c_null_char
  end function

    integer, intent(in) :: n_vert_levels

    c_config = f_to_c_string(config_path)

                            int(n_vert_levels, c_int), c_loc(error))
    this%n_cells = n_cells
    this%n_vert_levels = n_vert_levels

  subroutine miem_run(this, time_current, dt, air_density, layer_thickness, &
                      state, error)
    class(miem_t), intent(inout) :: this
    real(c_double), intent(in) :: time_current
    real(c_double), intent(in) :: dt
    real(c_double), intent(in), target :: air_density(:)
    real(c_double), intent(in), target :: layer_thickness(:)
    type(emis_state_t), intent(out) :: state
    type(error_t), intent(inout), target :: error

                           c_loc(air_density(1)), c_loc(layer_thickness(1)), &
                           n_atm, c_loc(error))

    type(error_t), intent(inout), target :: error

    character(len=64, kind=c_char), allocatable, target :: c_strings(:)
    integer :: i, n

    n = size(host_species)
    allocate(c_names(n))
    allocate(c_strings(n))

    do i = 1, n
      c_strings(i) = f_to_c_string(host_species(i))
      c_names(i) = c_loc(c_strings(i))

                                  int(n, c_int), c_loc(indices(1)), c_loc(error))
  end subroutine

    character(len=*), intent(in) :: config_path
    type(error_t), intent(inout), target :: error
    integer :: n

      call DeleteMIEM_c(this%ptr, c_loc(error))
      this%ptr = c_null_ptr
    end if
  end subroutine

The fix is to exclude yaml-cpp from the export requirements by not installing the export set's transitive dependencies — or more practically, since yaml-cpp and netCDF are `PRIVATE` and static, we need to handle the install differently.

cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.14)
project(MIEM
  VERSION 1.0.0
  LANGUAGES C CXX
  DESCRIPTION "Model Independent Emissions Module"
)

option(MIEM_BUILD_FORTRAN "Build Fortran bindings" ON)
option(MIEM_BUILD_TESTS "Build test suite" ON)
option(MIEM_DOUBLE_PRECISION "Use 64-bit floats" ON)

set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 17)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
set(CMAKE_CXX_EXTENSIONS OFF)

set(CMAKE_POSITION_INDEPENDENT_CODE ON)

if(MIEM_DOUBLE_PRECISION)
  add_compile_definitions(MIEM_USE_DOUBLE)
endif()

include(cmake/dependencies.cmake)

add_subdirectory(src)

if(MIEM_BUILD_FORTRAN)
  enable_language(Fortran)
  add_subdirectory(fortran)
endif()

if(MIEM_BUILD_TESTS)
  enable_testing()
  add_subdirectory(test)
endif()

# Install rules
install(TARGETS miem
  EXPORT MIEMTargets
  LIBRARY DESTINATION lib
  ARCHIVE DESTINATION lib
  INCLUDES DESTINATION include
)

install(DIRECTORY include/miem/ DESTINATION include/miem)

# Generate and install CMake package config
include(CMakePackageConfigHelpers)
write_basic_package_version_file(
  "${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/MIEMConfigVersion.cmake"
  VERSION ${PROJECT_VERSION}
  COMPATIBILITY SameMajorVersion
)

install(EXPORT MIEMTargets
  NAMESPACE musica::
  DESTINATION lib/cmake/MIEM
)

configure_file(
  "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/cmake/MIEMConfig.cmake.in"
  "${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/MIEMConfig.cmake"
  @ONLY
)

install(FILES
  "${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/MIEMConfig.cmake"
  "${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/MIEMConfigVersion.cmake"
  DESTINATION lib/cmake/MIEM
)

content.text:
`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
**The problem:** CMake's `install(EXPORT)` traces all link dependencies of exported targets — even `PRIVATE` ones — because a static library consumer needs to link the transitive deps at final link time. When yaml-cpp was fetched via FetchContent but not itself installed/exported, CMake can't resolve it in the export set.

**The fix:** Install yaml-cpp and netCDF into the same export set so CMake can find them, OR — the cleaner approach for a library like this — build `miem` as a `SHARED` library where `PRIVATE` deps are truly hidden, OR use `BUILD_SHARED_LIBS`. The most robust approach for HPC (where static is typical): install the FetchContent targets alongside MIEM.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

The cleanest fix: install yaml-cpp into the same export set when it was fetched by us, and have the config file re-find netCDF for consumers:

module miem_util_mod
  use iso_c_binding
  implicit none

  integer, parameter, public :: MIEM_MAX_NAME_LEN = 64

  ! Error type matching C MIEMError struct
  type, bind(C) :: error_t
    integer(c_int) :: code = 0
    character(kind=c_char) :: category(64) = c_null_char
    character(kind=c_char) :: message(256) = c_null_char
  end type error_t

contains

  function error_is_success(error) result(success)
    type(error_t), intent(in) :: error
    logical :: success
    success = (error%code == 0)
  end function

  function error_message(error) result(msg)
    type(error_t), intent(in) :: error
    character(len=255) :: msg
    integer :: i

    msg = ' '
    do i = 1, 255
      if (error%message(i) == c_null_char) exit
      msg(i:i) = error%message(i)
    end do
  end function

  function error_category(error) result(cat)
    type(error_t), intent(in) :: error
    character(len=63) :: cat
    integer :: i

    cat = ' '
    do i = 1, 63
      if (error%category(i) == c_null_char) exit
      cat(i:i) = error%category(i)
    end do
  end function

## Consensus: Architecture is sound, issues are in boundary layers

All reviewers agreed the three-layer architecture (C++ → C API → Fortran), EmissionSource extensibility, and DatasetDescriptor pattern are well-designed. Issues are concentrated in:

### P0 — Critical (flagged by 3-4 reviewers)

module miem_mod
  use iso_c_binding
  use miem_util_mod
  use miem_emis_state_mod
  implicit none
  private

  type, public :: miem_t
    type(c_ptr), private :: ptr = c_null_ptr
    integer :: n_cells = 0
    integer :: n_vert_levels = 0
  contains
    procedure :: init => miem_init
    procedure :: run => miem_run
    procedure :: resolve_host_indices => miem_resolve_host_indices
    procedure :: num_species => miem_num_species
    procedure :: finalize => miem_finalize
  end type miem_t

  public :: miem_query_species_count

  ! C function interfaces
  interface
    function CreateMIEM_c(config_path, n_cells, n_vert_levels, error) &
        bind(C, name="CreateMIEM")
      import :: c_ptr, c_char, c_int
      character(kind=c_char), intent(in) :: config_path(*)
      integer(c_int), value :: n_cells
      integer(c_int), value :: n_vert_levels
      type(c_ptr), value :: error
      type(c_ptr) :: CreateMIEM_c
    end function

    subroutine DeleteMIEM_c(miem, error) bind(C, name="DeleteMIEM")
      import :: c_ptr
      type(c_ptr), value :: miem
      type(c_ptr), value :: error
    end subroutine

    function MIEMRun_c(miem, time, dt, air_density, layer_thickness, &
        n_atm_elements, error) bind(C, name="MIEMRun")
      import :: c_ptr, c_double, c_int
      type(c_ptr), value :: miem
      real(c_double), value :: time
      real(c_double), value :: dt
      type(c_ptr), value :: air_density
      type(c_ptr), value :: layer_thickness
      integer(c_int), value :: n_atm_elements
      type(c_ptr), value :: error
      type(c_ptr) :: MIEMRun_c
    end function

    subroutine MIEMResolveHostIndices_c(miem, host_names, n_host, indices, error) &
        bind(C, name="MIEMResolveHostIndices")
      import :: c_ptr, c_int
      type(c_ptr), value :: miem
      type(c_ptr), value :: host_names
      integer(c_int), value :: n_host
      type(c_ptr), value :: indices
      type(c_ptr), value :: error
    end subroutine

    function MIEMGetNumSpecies_c(miem) bind(C, name="MIEMGetNumSpecies")
      import :: c_ptr, c_int
      type(c_ptr), value :: miem
      integer(c_int) :: MIEMGetNumSpecies_c
    end function

    function MIEMQuerySpeciesCount_c(config_path, error) &
        bind(C, name="MIEMQuerySpeciesCount")
      import :: c_ptr, c_char, c_int
      character(kind=c_char), intent(in) :: config_path(*)
      type(c_ptr), value :: error
      integer(c_int) :: MIEMQuerySpeciesCount_c
    end function

    subroutine MIEMQuerySpeciesNames_c(config_path, names, max_names, error) &
        bind(C, name="MIEMQuerySpeciesNames")
      import :: c_ptr, c_char, c_int
      character(kind=c_char), intent(in) :: config_path(*)
      type(c_ptr), value :: names
      integer(c_int), value :: max_names
      type(c_ptr), value :: error
    end subroutine
  end interface

contains

  subroutine miem_init(this, config_path, n_cells, n_vert_levels, error)
    class(miem_t), intent(inout) :: this
    character(len=*), intent(in) :: config_path
    integer, intent(in) :: n_cells
    integer, intent(in) :: n_vert_levels
    type(error_t), intent(inout), target :: error

    character(len=len_trim(config_path)+1, kind=c_char) :: c_config

    c_config = f_to_c_string(config_path)
    this%ptr = CreateMIEM_c(c_config, int(n_cells, c_int), &
                            int(n_vert_levels, c_int), c_loc(error))
    this%n_cells = n_cells
    this%n_vert_levels = n_vert_levels
  end subroutine

  subroutine miem_run(this, time_current, dt, air_density, layer_thickness, &
                      state, error)
    class(miem_t), intent(inout) :: this
    real(c_double), intent(in) :: time_current
    real(c_double), intent(in) :: dt
    real(c_double), intent(in), target :: air_density(:)
    real(c_double), intent(in), target :: layer_thickness(:)
    type(emis_state_t), intent(out) :: state
    type(error_t), intent(inout), target :: error

    integer(c_int) :: n_atm

    type(c_ptr) :: state_ptr

    n_atm = int(size(air_density), c_int)
    state_ptr = MIEMRun_c(this%ptr, time_current, dt, &
                           c_loc(air_density(1)), c_loc(layer_thickness(1)), &
                           n_atm, c_loc(error))
    call state%set_ptr(state_ptr)

    if (error_is_success(error) .and. state%is_associated()) then
      call state%update_references()
    end if
  end subroutine

  subroutine miem_resolve_host_indices(this, host_species, indices, error)
    class(miem_t), intent(inout) :: this
    character(len=*), intent(in) :: host_species(:)
    integer(c_int), intent(out), target :: indices(:)
    type(error_t), intent(inout), target :: error

    type(c_ptr), allocatable, target :: c_names(:)
    character(len=MIEM_MAX_NAME_LEN, kind=c_char), allocatable, target :: c_strings(:)
    integer :: i, n

    n = size(host_species)
    allocate(c_names(n))
    allocate(c_strings(n))

    do i = 1, n
      c_strings(i) = f_to_c_string(host_species(i))
      c_names(i) = c_loc(c_strings(i))
    end do

    call MIEMResolveHostIndices_c(this%ptr, c_loc(c_names(1)), &
                                  int(n, c_int), c_loc(indices(1)), c_loc(error))
  end subroutine

  function miem_num_species(this) result(n)
    class(miem_t), intent(in) :: this
    integer :: n
    n = MIEMGetNumSpecies_c(this%ptr)
  end function

  function miem_query_species_count(config_path, error) result(n)
    character(len=*), intent(in) :: config_path
    type(error_t), intent(inout), target :: error
    integer :: n

    character(len=len_trim(config_path)+1, kind=c_char) :: c_config

    c_config = f_to_c_string(config_path)
    n = MIEMQuerySpeciesCount_c(c_config, c_loc(error))
  end function

  subroutine miem_finalize(this, error)
    class(miem_t), intent(inout) :: this
    type(error_t), intent(inout), target :: error

    if (c_associated(this%ptr)) then
      call DeleteMIEM_c(this%ptr, c_loc(error))
      this%ptr = c_null_ptr
    end if
  end subroutine

end module miem_mod

      call state%update_references()
    end if
  end subroutine

  subroutine miem_resolve_host_indices(this, host_species, indices, error)
    class(miem_t), intent(inout) :: this
    character(len=*), intent(in) :: host_species(:)
    integer(c_int), intent(out), target :: indices(:)
    type(error_t), intent(inout), target :: error

    type(c_ptr), allocatable, target :: c_names(:)
    character(len=MIEM_MAX_NAME_LEN, kind=c_char), allocatable, target :: c_strings(:)
    integer :: i, n

    n = size(host_species)
    allocate(c_names(n))
    allocate(c_strings(n))

    do i = 1, n
      c_strings(i) = f_to_c_string(host_species(i))
      c_names(i) = c_loc(c_strings(i))
    end do

    call MIEMResolveHostIndices_c(this%ptr, c_loc(c_names(1)), &
                                  int(n, c_int), c_loc(indices(1)), c_loc(error))
  end subroutine

  function miem_num_species(this) result(n)
    class(miem_t), intent(in) :: this
    integer :: n
    n = MIEMGetNumSpecies_c(this%ptr)
  end function

  function miem_query_species_count(config_path, error) result(n)
    character(len=*), intent(in) :: config_path
    type(error_t), intent(inout), target :: error
    integer :: n

    character(len=len_trim(config_path)+1, kind=c_char) :: c_config

    c_config = f_to_c_string(config_path)
    n = MIEMQuerySpeciesCount_c(c_config, c_loc(error))
  end function

  subroutine miem_finalize(this, error)
    class(miem_t), intent(inout) :: this
    type(error_t), intent(inout), target :: error

    if (c_associated(this%ptr)) then
      call DeleteMIEM_c(this%ptr, c_loc(error))
      this%ptr = c_null_ptr
    end if
  end subroutine

end module miem_mod

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main, develop]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main, develop]

jobs:
  build-and-test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      matrix:
        compiler: [gcc]
        build_type: [Debug, Release]

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y \
            cmake \
            g++ \
            gfortran \
            libnetcdf-dev \
            libnetcdff-dev

      - name: Configure
        env:
          BUILD_TYPE: ${{ matrix.build_type }}
        run: |
          cmake -B build \
            -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE="${BUILD_TYPE}" \
            -DMIEM_BUILD_FORTRAN=ON \
            -DMIEM_BUILD_TESTS=ON

      - name: Build
        run: cmake --build build -j$(nproc)

      - name: Test
        run: cd build && ctest --output-on-failure

cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.14)
project(MIEM
  VERSION 1.0.0
  LANGUAGES C CXX
  DESCRIPTION "Model Independent Emissions Module"
)

option(MIEM_BUILD_FORTRAN "Build Fortran bindings" ON)
option(MIEM_BUILD_TESTS "Build test suite" ON)
option(MIEM_DOUBLE_PRECISION "Use 64-bit floats" ON)

set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 17)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
set(CMAKE_CXX_EXTENSIONS OFF)

set(CMAKE_POSITION_INDEPENDENT_CODE ON)

if(MIEM_DOUBLE_PRECISION)
  add_compile_definitions(MIEM_USE_DOUBLE)
endif()

include(cmake/dependencies.cmake)

add_subdirectory(src)

if(MIEM_BUILD_FORTRAN)
  enable_language(Fortran)
  add_subdirectory(fortran)
endif()

if(MIEM_BUILD_TESTS)
  enable_testing()
  add_subdirectory(test)
endif()

# Install rules
set(MIEM_INSTALL_TARGETS miem)

# If we fetched yaml-cpp via FetchContent, it must be in the export set
# because CMake traces static library PRIVATE deps during install(EXPORT).
if(MIEM_FETCHED_YAML_CPP)
  list(APPEND MIEM_INSTALL_TARGETS yaml-cpp)
endif()

install(TARGETS ${MIEM_INSTALL_TARGETS}
  EXPORT MIEMTargets
  LIBRARY DESTINATION lib
  ARCHIVE DESTINATION lib
  INCLUDES DESTINATION include
)

install(DIRECTORY include/miem/ DESTINATION include/miem)

# Generate and install CMake package config
include(CMakePackageConfigHelpers)
write_basic_package_version_file(
  "${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/MIEMConfigVersion.cmake"
  VERSION ${PROJECT_VERSION}
  COMPATIBILITY SameMajorVersion
)

install(EXPORT MIEMTargets
  NAMESPACE musica::
  DESTINATION lib/cmake/MIEM
)

configure_file(
  "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/cmake/MIEMConfig.cmake.in"
  "${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/MIEMConfig.cmake"
  @ONLY
)

install(FILES
  "${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/MIEMConfig.cmake"
  "${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/MIEMConfigVersion.cmake"
  DESTINATION lib/cmake/MIEM
)

# Install FindnetCDF.cmake so downstream consumers can re-find netCDF
install(FILES
  "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/cmake/FindnetCDF.cmake"
  DESTINATION lib/cmake/MIEM
)

file.content:
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main, develop]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main, develop]

jobs:
  build-and-test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - build_type: Debug
            double_precision: ON
            fortran: ON
          - build_type: Release
            double_precision: ON
            fortran: ON
          - build_type: Release
            double_precision: OFF
            fortran: OFF

    name: "${{ matrix.build_type }} (double=${{ matrix.double_precision }}, fortran=${{ matrix.fortran }})"

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install dependencies
        env:
          INSTALL_FORTRAN: ${{ matrix.fortran }}
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y cmake g++ libnetcdf-dev
          if [ "$INSTALL_FORTRAN" = "ON" ]; then
            sudo apt-get install -y gfortran libnetcdff-dev
          fi

      - name: Configure
        env:
          BUILD_TYPE: ${{ matrix.build_type }}
          DOUBLE_PREC: ${{ matrix.double_precision }}
          BUILD_FORTRAN: ${{ matrix.fortran }}
        run: |
          cmake -B build \
            -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE="$BUILD_TYPE" \
            -DMIEM_BUILD_FORTRAN="$BUILD_FORTRAN" \
            -DMIEM_DOUBLE_PRECISION="$DOUBLE_PREC" \
            -DMIEM_BUILD_TESTS=ON

      - name: Build
        run: cmake --build build -j$(nproc)

      - name: Test
        run: cd build && ctest --output-on-failure

content.text:
`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
The `static_assert` in the C interface files acts as a compile-time gate: the C/Fortran boundary **must** use double precision because Fortran `real(c_double)` and C `double` are the same type. Single-precision builds can still use the C++ core directly (e.g., from another C++ module), but they cannot use the C API. By conditionally excluding the C API sources, we make this constraint explicit in the build system rather than having CI silently fail.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

We should also guard the Fortran build behind double precision, since the Fortran bindings call the C API.

content.text:
`miem_c_interface.cpp` includes both `error_handling.hpp` and `miem_c.h` directly. Since `error_handling.hpp` now includes `miem_c.h`, and `miem_c.h` has `#ifndef MIEM_C_H` include guards, the second include is harmless — `#pragma once` and `#ifndef` guards will prevent double inclusion. No conflict.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
The root cause: C and C++ have different struct declaration semantics. In C, `struct MIEM_Error { ... };` creates a *tag* named `MIEM_Error` that must be referenced as `struct MIEM_Error`. The `typedef struct { ... } MIEM_Error;` pattern creates an *anonymous* struct with a typedef alias. In C++, both forms define a type named `MIEM_Error`, but they're technically different types — one is `struct MIEM_Error`, the other is an unnamed struct. The fix is the classic one: single definition in one header, everyone else includes it.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

This should resolve the build error. The `MIEM_Error` type is now defined exclusively in `miem_c.h`.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate test NetCDF files for MIEM unit tests."""

import numpy as np

try:
    from netCDF4 import Dataset
except ImportError:
    print("netCDF4 not installed. Install with: pip install netCDF4")
    exit(1)


def create_ces_compliant_file(filepath, n_cells=10, n_times=2):
    """Create a CES-compliant emissions file."""
    ds = Dataset(filepath, "w", format="NETCDF4")

    # Global attributes (CES compliance)
    ds.miem_version = "1.0"
    ds.emission_sector = "anthropogenic"
    ds.inventory_id = "TEST-INV-v1"

    # Dimensions
    ds.createDimension("Time", n_times)
    ds.createDimension("nCells", n_cells)

    # Time variable
    time_var = ds.createVariable("Time", "f8", ("Time",))
    time_var[:] = np.arange(n_times, dtype=np.float64) * 86400.0  # Daily

    # Emission species
    species = {"NOx": 1e-9, "SO2": 5e-10, "CO": 2e-8}
    for name, base_flux in species.items():
        var = ds.createVariable(f"emi_{name}", "f8", ("Time", "nCells"))
        var.units = "kg m-2 s-1"
        # Vary by cell and time
        for t in range(n_times):
            var[t, :] = base_flux * (1 + 0.1 * np.arange(n_cells)) * (1 + 0.05 * t)

    ds.close()
    print(f"Created CES-compliant file: {filepath}")


def create_non_ces_file(filepath, n_cells=10, n_times=2):
    """Create a non-CES file (requires descriptor)."""
    ds = Dataset(filepath, "w", format="NETCDF4")

    # No miem_version attribute — not CES-compliant
    ds.source = "FINN v2.5"

    # Dimensions (non-standard names)
    ds.createDimension("time", n_times)
    ds.createDimension("ncol", n_cells)

    # Time variable
    time_var = ds.createVariable("time", "f8", ("time",))
    time_var[:] = np.arange(n_times, dtype=np.float64) * 86400.0

    # Non-standard variable names
    species = {"fire_NOx": 1e15, "fire_CO": 5e16}
    for name, base_flux in species.items():
        var = ds.createVariable(name, "f8", ("time", "ncol"))
        var.units = "molecules cm-2 s-1"
        for t in range(n_times):
            var[t, :] = base_flux * (1 + 0.2 * np.arange(n_cells)) * (1 + 0.1 * t)

    ds.close()
    print(f"Created non-CES file: {filepath}")


if __name__ == "__main__":

    test_data_dir = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "..", "test", "data")
    os.makedirs(test_data_dir, exist_ok=True)

    create_ces_compliant_file(os.path.join(test_data_dir, "test_anthro.nc"))
    create_non_ces_file(os.path.join(test_data_dir, "test_fire.nc"))

Good catch. These scripts are encoding a **de facto CES specification** that we said wasn't fully defined yet. Here's what they reveal:

**`generate_test_data.py`** creates two kinds of test fixtures:
- A "CES-compliant" file with specific conventions: `miem_version` global attribute, `Time`/`nCells` dimensions, `emi_` variable prefix, `kg m-2 s-1` units
- A "non-CES" file (simulating FINN data) with different dimension names, variable prefixes, and units — demonstrating the DatasetDescriptor path

**`validate_ces.py`** is a standalone validator that checks files against those same CES conventions:
- Requires `miem_version` global attribute
- Requires `Time` and `nCells` dimensions
- Requires `emi_*` variable prefix
- Expects `(Time, nCells)` dimension ordering
- Expects `kg m-2 s-1` units

So despite our earlier decision that "CES" isn't a formally defined external standard, these scripts **are** defining one — they're just doing it implicitly through code rather than through documentation. The conventions they encode are:

| Convention | Value |
|---|---|
| Compliance marker | `miem_version` global attribute |
| Time dimension | `Time` |
| Cell dimension | `nCells` |
| Variable prefix | `emi_` |
| Expected units | `kg m-2 s-1` |
| Variable layout | `(Time, nCells)` |

This is exactly what the `CESReader::DetectFormat()` and `DiscoverSpecies()` code checks for on the C++ side.

These scripts are internally consistent with the C++ reader, but they contradict our decision to avoid prematurely naming/formalizing the format. There are a few options:

1. **Keep them as-is but rename** — call them what they are: `generate_test_data.py` is fine, but `validate_ces.py` could become `validate_miem_input.py` to align with the "input convention" framing
2. **Formalize the convention** — since we clearly *do* have a specification (it's just scattered across code), document it and own it
3. **Defer** — leave them alone until the preprocessing tool scope is clearer, then decide on naming

What's your preference?

Excellent! Now I have a complete picture. Let me create a comprehensive analysis report.

---

## MIEM Input Data Requirements Analysis

Based on thorough tracing of the data flow from file read through EmisState output, here is what MIEM actually needs from input data:

### 1. CESReader — Dimensions, Variables, and Attributes

**Mandatory Dimensions:**
- `Time` (CES default) or custom via `DatasetDescriptor.time_dimension`
  - Can be absent: defaults to single time step (n_time_steps = 1)
  - Type: unlimited integer dimension in NetCDF
- `nCells` (CES default) or custom via `DatasetDescriptor.cell_dimension`
  - Must exist; throws IOError if missing
  - Stores the horizontal grid cell count

**Mandatory Variables:**
- `Time` or custom time variable (by dimension name)
  - Data type: double (via `nc_get_var_double`)
  - Attributes:
    - `units`: CF Conventions time units string (e.g., "seconds since 1970-01-01" or "days since 2000-01-01 12:00:00")
    - Parsed via regex: `(\w+)\s+since\s+(\d{4})-(\d{1,2})-(\d{1,2})(?:\s+(\d{1,2}):(\d{1,2})(?::(\d{1,2}))?)?`
    - Supports units: seconds, minutes, hours, days
    - Returned as seconds since Unix epoch (double)

**Species Flux Variables:**
- Named pattern: `emi_<species>` (CES default) or custom prefix via `DatasetDescriptor.variable_prefix`
- Example: `emi_NOx`, `emi_SO2`, `emi_CO`
- Data types: NC_DOUBLE or NC_FLOAT (auto-detected at compile time via `MIEM_USE_DOUBLE`)
- **Dimensionality (auto-detected):**
  - 2D: `(Time, nCells)` — multiple time steps, data sliced by time_index
  - 1D: `(nCells)` — single snapshot, same data returned for any time_index
- Layout: row-major (NetCDF C default)
- Missing values:
  - Checked for `_FillValue` attribute
  - Masked to 0.0 if match detected

**Global Attributes:**
- `miem_version`: determines CES compliance
  - If present and readable: `is_ces_compliant = true`, ignores descriptor overrides
  - If absent: uses descriptor overrides

**Minimum Viable CES NetCDF File Structure:**
```
dimensions:
  Time = 1 ;           // or any N > 0
  nCells = 100 ;       // any N > 0
variables:
  double Time(Time) ;
    Time:units = "seconds since 1970-01-01" ;
  double emi_NOx(Time, nCells) ;
  double emi_SO2(Time, nCells) ;
attributes:
  :miem_version = "1.0" ;
```

---

### 2. DatasetDescriptor — What Varies Across Sources

The descriptor struct allows MIEM to read non-CES-compliant files by normalizing them:

```cpp
struct DatasetDescriptor {
  std::string variable_prefix = "emi_";         // Override variable prefix
  std::string flux_units = "kg m-2 s-1";        // Metadata (stored, not used)
  Real unit_conversion_factor = 1.0;            // Multiply raw data by this
  std::string time_dimension = "Time";          // Dimension name override
  std::string cell_dimension = "nCells";        // Dimension name override
  std::map<std::string, std::string> species_rename;  // Variable name mapping
};
```

**Fields that actually matter for reading:**
- `time_dimension`: looked up in file via `nc_inq_dimid()`
- `cell_dimension`: looked up in file via `nc_inq_dimid()`
- `variable_prefix`: used to detect species variables in file
- `species_rename`: bidirectional map for canonical name discovery and flux reading

# Atmospheric Emissions Inventory Research

Below is a comprehensive summary of the major emissions inventories used in the MUSICA/CESM/CAM-chem/WRF-Chem/GEOS-Chem ecosystem. This is based on established knowledge of these datasets as used in the NCAR/ACOM community.

---

## 1. CEDS (Community Emissions Data System)

- **Provider**: Joint Global Change Research Institute (JGCRI) / Pacific Northwest National Laboratory (PNNL), developed for CMIP6
- **File format**: NetCDF-4 (CF-compliant). Distributed via ESGIS/input4MIPs for CMIP6.
- **Grid/spatial representation**: Regular lat/lon, typically 0.5° x 0.5° global grid. Dimensions usually `lat`, `lon`.
- **Time representation**: Monthly fields from 1750–2014 (historical) with extensions. Time dimension `time`, units typically `days since ...` with a standard or no-leap calendar. Annual totals also available.
- **Variable naming conventions**: Variables named by species with sector suffix, e.g., `SO2_em_anthro`, `BC_em_anthro`, or by species alone with sector as a dimension. In input4MIPs files: `{species}_em_{sector}` pattern. Sector names: `AGR`, `ENE`, `IND`, `TRA`, `RCO`, `SLV`, `WST`, `SHP`.
- **Units**: `kg m-2 s-1` (mass flux per unit area per second) — the standard CF/CMIP6 convention.
- **Sector breakdown**: 8 sectors (agriculture, energy, industry, transportation, residential/commercial, solvents, waste, international shipping). Sectors can appear as separate variables within a single file or as a sector dimension. CMIP6 input4MIPs files typically use one file per species with sectors as separate variables.
- **Species coverage**: SO2, NOx, CO, NMVOC, NH3, BC, OC, CH4. VOC speciation files break NMVOCs into individual species (e.g., ethane, propane, formaldehyde, toluene, xylenes, etc.).

---

## 2. EDGAR (Emissions Database for Global Atmospheric Research)

- **Provider**: European Commission Joint Research Centre (JRC) / Netherlands Environmental Assessment Agency (PBL)
- **File format**: NetCDF-4. Older versions also distributed as text/ASCII grids. Current versions (v6.1, v7.0, v8.0) are NetCDF.
- **Grid/spatial representation**: Regular lat/lon at 0.1° x 0.1° (newer versions) or 0.5° x 0.5° (older). Dimensions: `lat`, `lon`.
- **Time representation**: Annual or monthly. Time dimension `time`. Annual files contain one timestep per year. Monthly files have 12 timesteps. Coverage from 1970 to ~2–3 years prior to release.
- **Variable naming conventions**: Typically the variable is named `emi_{species}` or simply the species name (e.g., `NOx`, `SO2`, `CO`). Filenames encode sector and species, e.g., `v8.0_FT2022_GHG_CO2_excl_short-cycle_org_C_2022_TOTALS.0.1x0.1.nc`.
- **Units**: `kg m-2 s-1` in processed versions for models. Raw EDGAR data often in `kg/m2/s` or `ton/year/cell` depending on product.
- **Sector breakdown**: IPCC 1996/2006 sector codes (e.g., `1A1` for energy industries, `1A3b` for road transport). Distributed as separate files per sector, or with a `TOTALS` aggregate file.
- **Species coverage**: CO2, CH4, N2O, SO2, NOx, CO, NMVOC, NH3, BC, OC, PM2.5, PM10, and fluorinated gases.

---

## 3. FINN (Fire INventory from NCAR)

- **Provider**: NCAR/ACOM (Christine Wiedinmyer et al.)
- **File format**: Historically CSV/text (FINN v1, v1.5). FINN v2.5 provides NetCDF-4 files and also CSV. For CAM-chem, data is regridded to NetCDF on model grids.
- **Grid/spatial representation**: Originally point-source (individual fire detections from MODIS/VIIRS with lat/lon coordinates). For model input, regridded to regular lat/lon (e.g., 1° x 1° or 0.9° x 1.25° for CAM-chem). The raw data has `LONGI`, `LATI` columns.
- **Time representation**: Daily. One record per fire per day. NetCDF files use `time` dimension with `days since` reference. Coverage: 2002–present (MODIS), 2012–present (VIIRS).
- **Variable naming conventions**: In CSV: columns like `CO`, `NO`, `SO2`, `PM25`, `OC`, `BC`, `NH3`, `NMOC`, etc. In NetCDF for CAM-chem: `bb` prefix or `fire_` prefix, e.g., `fire_CO`, `bb_CO`, or species names matching the chemical mechanism (MOZART/SAPRC).
- **Units**: Raw CSV: `kg/day` per fire pixel. NetCDF for models: `molecules/cm2/s` (for gas-phase) or `kg m-2 s-1` (for aerosols), depending on the model interface.
- **Sector breakdown**: Single sector (open biomass burning). Vegetation type information is included (grassland, tropical forest, temperate forest, boreal forest, shrubland, cropland) but typically as metadata, not separate files.
- **Species coverage**: CO, CO2, NO, NO2, SO2, NH3, PM2.5, PM10, OC, BC, CH4, and speciated NMVOCs (~50+ species mapped to chemical mechanisms like MOZART-T1, SAPRC99, GEOS-Chem).

---

## 4. GFED (Global Fire Emissions Database)

- **Provider**: Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam / NASA (Guido van der Werf et al.)
- **File format**: HDF5 (`.hdf5`) for the main product. NetCDF versions are also available (converted for model use). GFED4/4s is the current version.
- **Grid/spatial representation**: Regular lat/lon at 0.25° x 0.25°. Dimensions: `lat`, `lon` (720 x 1440).
- **Time representation**: Monthly base fields with daily and 3-hourly scale factors for temporal downscaling. Time: `month` within annual files, daily fractions in separate files. Coverage: 1997–present.
- **Variable naming conventions**: In HDF5: organized by groups, e.g., `/emissions/{month}/C` for carbon emissions, `/emissions/{month}/DM` for dry matter burned. Partitioning tables convert total carbon to species. Basis fields are `DM` (dry matter) or total carbon `C`, then emission factors convert to individual species.
- **Units**: Base product: `kg DM m-2 month-1` (dry matter burned) or `g C m-2 month-1`. After applying emission factors: `kg species m-2 s-1` for model input.
- **Sector breakdown**: 6 source types as separate fields: `SAVA` (savanna), `BORF` (boreal forest), `TEMF` (temperate forest), `DEFO` (tropical deforestation), `PEAT` (peatland), `AGRI` (agricultural waste burning). These are provided as fractional contributions.
- **Species coverage**: Via emission factor tables: CO2, CO, CH4, NMHC, H2, NOx, N2O, PM2.5, TPM, TPC, OC, BC, SO2, and individual VOC species (with chemical mechanism mappings).

---

## 5. MEGAN (Model of Emissions of Gases and Aerosols from Nature)

- **Provider**: NCAR/ACOM (Alex Guenther et al.). MEGAN is actually an emissions model, not just an inventory — it computes biogenic emissions online using meteorology and land surface data.
- **File format**: Input data files in NetCDF-4 (emission factor maps, LAI, PFT distributions). When used to produce offline emissions, output is NetCDF.
- **Grid/spatial representation**: Input emission factor maps at various resolutions (e.g., 0.5° x 0.5° for CLM-based PFT data). In CESM, MEGAN runs inline with CLM at the model's land grid resolution (FV or SE unstructured).
- **Time representation**: Emission factor maps are static (climatological). LAI inputs are monthly climatology. Online calculation produces emissions at the model timestep. Offline MEGAN output can be hourly or monthly.
- **Variable naming conventions**: Emission factor variables: `ef_{species}` or `EF_ISOP`, `EF_MBO`, `EF_MYRC`, etc. In CLM/CESM: `MEGANvoc_emis_{species}`, or mapped to mechanism species. Standard MEGAN compound classes: isoprene, monoterpenes (alpha-pinene, beta-pinene, myrcene, limonene, etc.), sesquiterpenes, methanol, ethanol, acetaldehyde, acetone, etc.
- **Units**: Emission factors: `ug m-2 hr-1` at standard conditions (30°C, 1000 umol/m2/s PAR). Computed emissions: `molecules/cm2/s` or `kg m-2 s-1` depending on the model interface.
- **Sector breakdown**: Single sector (biogenic). Sub-categories by compound class or PFT type.
- **Species coverage**: ~150 compounds. Key species: isoprene (dominant), monoterpenes (alpha-pinene, beta-pinene, limonene, myrcene, ocimene, sabinene, 3-carene, etc.), sesquiterpenes, oxygenated VOCs (methanol, ethanol, formaldehyde, acetaldehyde, formic acid, acetic acid, acetone), 2-methyl-3-buten-2-ol (MBO), and others. These are mapped to lumped mechanism species for different chemical mechanisms.

---

## 6. CAMS-GLOB-ANT (Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service Global Anthropogenic)

- **Provider**: ECMWF / Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service. Builds on EDGAR and other regional inventories.
- **File format**: NetCDF-4 (CF-compliant). Distributed via the Copernicus Atmosphere Data Store (ADS).
- **Grid/spatial representation**: Regular lat/lon at 0.1° x 0.1° global. Dimensions: `latitude`, `longitude` (note: ECMWF convention uses `latitude`/`longitude` rather than `lat`/`lon`).
- **Time representation**: Monthly. Time dimension `time`. Coverage: 2000–present (updated annually, ~2 year lag).
- **Variable naming conventions**: Species names as variable names, e.g., `co`, `nox`, `so2`, `nh3`, `nmvoc`, `bc`, `oc`, `pm2p5`, `pm10`, `ch4`, `co2`. Note lowercase convention. Files per sector.
- **Units**: `kg m-2 s-1`.
- **Sector breakdown**: Sectors distributed as separate files or with sector dimension. ---

## 7. HTAP (Hemispheric Transport of Air Pollution)

- **Provider**: HTAP initiative (UNECE/WMO Task Force). HTAPv2 and HTAPv3 are the key products.
- **File format**: NetCDF-4 (CF-compliant).
- **Grid/spatial representation**: Regular lat/lon at 0.1° x 0.1° (HTAPv2/v3). Dimensions: `lat`, `lon`.
- **Time representation**: Monthly. 12 timesteps per file. HTAPv2 is a 2008 and 2010 base year. HTAPv3 extends coverage. Time dimension `time` with `days since` reference.
- **Variable naming conventions**: Variables named `{species}_em_{sector}` or `{species}_{sector}`. Example: `NOx_em_ENERGY`, `SO2_em_INDUSTRY`. Filenames encode the species.
- **Units**: `kg m-2 s-1`.
- **Sector breakdown**: Sectors as separate variables or files: `AIR` (aircraft), `SHIPS`, `ENERGY`, `INDUSTRY`, `TRANSPORT`, `RESIDENTIAL`, `AGRICULTURE`, `WASTE`, plus natural/biomass burning sources in some configurations.
- **Species coverage**: SO2, NOx, CO, NMVOC, NH3, BC, OC, PM2.5, PM10, CH4. VOC speciation tables available.

---

## 8. GOCART-2G (relevant to MUSICA/MusicBox)

- **Provider**: NASA GMAO (Arlindo da Silva et al.), used in GEOS/GEOS-Chem and being integrated into MUSICA.
- **File format**: NetCDF-4 (COARDS/CF compliant). Historically also in GEOS binary format (now deprecated).
- **Grid/spatial representation**: Regular lat/lon at various resolutions (2° x 2.5°, 1° x 1.25°, 0.5° x 0.625° matching GEOS grids). Can also operate on cubed-sphere grids in GEOS. Dimensions: `lat`, `lon`, `lev` (for 3D sources like aviation).
- **Time representation**: Monthly climatology or time-varying monthly. Some fields are daily (e.g., biomass burning from QFED). Time dimension `time`. Files typically contain 12 monthly records.
- **Variable naming conventions**: Species-specific variables with GOCART naming, e.g., `DU` (dust, with size bins `DU001`–`DU005`), `SS` (sea salt), `SO2`, `SO4`, `BC`, `OC`, `DMS`, `CO`. Biomass burning variables: `biomass_{species}`. Emission variables use `EMI` prefix in some configurations.
- **Units**: `kg m-2 s-1` for surface fluxes. Some products use `kg/m2/s`.
- **Sector breakdown**: Separate files for different source types: anthropogenic, biomass burning (QFED, GFED), biogenic, dust, sea salt, volcanic (continuous degassing and eruptive). The 2G (second generation) version reorganizes around a component-based architecture.
- **Species coverage**: Primarily aerosol-focused: dust (5 size bins), sea salt (5 size bins), sulfate (SO2, SO4, DMS, MSA), carbonaceous (BC, OC, brown carbon in 2G), CO. Coupling to full chemistry via GEOS-Chem.

---

## Summary Table of Key Format Properties

| Inventory | Format | Resolution | Time | Units | Sector Method |
|-----------|--------|-----------|------|-------|--------------|
| CEDS | NC4 | 0.5° | Monthly | kg/m2/s | Separate variables |
| EDGAR | NC4/HDF5 | 0.1° | Annual/Monthly | kg/m2/s | Separate files |
| FINN | CSV/NC4 | Point/regridded | Daily | kg/day or molec/cm2/s | Single (fire) |
| GFED | HDF5/NC4 | 0.25° | Monthly+daily scaling | kg DM/m2/month | 6 fire types |
| MEGAN | NC4 (inputs) | 0.5° (inputs) | Online/climatology | ug/m2/hr (EFs) | Single (biogenic) |
| CAMS-GLOB | NC4 | 0.1° | Monthly | kg/m2/s | Separate files |
| HTAP | NC4 | 0.1° | Monthly | kg/m2/s | Separate vars/files |
| GOCART-2G | NC4 | Various | Monthly/daily | kg/m2/s | Separate files |

## Key Design Implications for MIEM

1. **NetCDF is universal**: Every major inventory uses NetCDF-4 (or HDF5 which NetCDF-4 reads). The NetCDF-C API is the right choice.

2. **Units are mostly standardized**: `kg m-2 s-1` is the dominant unit for model-ready data. MIEM should expect this as the default and support conversion from common alternatives (`molecules/cm2/s`, `kg/day`, `kg/grid-cell/month`).

3. **Dimension naming varies**: `lat`/`lon` vs `latitude`/`longitude` vs `XLAT`/`XLONG`. MIEM's config-driven approach should let users specify dimension names.

4. **Species naming varies widely**: No standard naming convention across inventories. Config-based species mapping (inventory name to model name) is essential.

5. **Sector handling varies**: Some use separate files, some use separate variables, some use a sector dimension. MIEM needs to handle at least "separate files" and "separate variables" patterns.

6. **Temporal resolution varies**: Monthly is most common, but daily (FINN) and sub-daily scaling (GFED) exist. Temporal interpolation between monthly values is a baseline requirement.

7. **Grid resolution varies**: From 0.1° to 2.5°. MIEM itself doesn't need to regrid (the host model handles that), but it needs to read various grid sizes efficiently.

# Atmospheric Emissions Inventory Research

Below is a comprehensive summary of the major emissions inventories used in the MUSICA/CESM/CAM-chem/WRF-Chem/GEOS-Chem ecosystem. This is based on established knowledge of these datasets as used in the NCAR/ACOM community.

---

## 1. CEDS (Community Emissions Data System)

- **Provider**: Joint Global Change Research Institute (JGCRI) / Pacific Northwest National Laboratory (PNNL), developed for CMIP6
- **File format**: NetCDF-4 (CF-compliant). Distributed via ESGIS/input4MIPs for CMIP6.
- **Grid/spatial representation**: Regular lat/lon, typically 0.5° x 0.5° global grid. Dimensions usually `lat`, `lon`.
- **Time representation**: Monthly fields from 1750–2014 (historical) with extensions. Time dimension `time`, units typically `days since ...` with a standard or no-leap calendar. Annual totals also available.
- **Variable naming conventions**: Variables named by species with sector suffix, e.g., `SO2_em_anthro`, `BC_em_anthro`, or by species alone with sector as a dimension. In input4MIPs files: `{species}_em_{sector}` pattern. Sector names: `AGR`, `ENE`, `IND`, `TRA`, `RCO`, `SLV`, `WST`, `SHP`.
- **Units**: `kg m-2 s-1` (mass flux per unit area per second) — the standard CF/CMIP6 convention.
- **Sector breakdown**: 8 sectors (agriculture, energy, industry, transportation, residential/commercial, solvents, waste, international shipping). Sectors can appear as separate variables within a single file or as a sector dimension. CMIP6 input4MIPs files typically use one file per species with sectors as separate variables.
- **Species coverage**: SO2, NOx, CO, NMVOC, NH3, BC, OC, CH4. VOC speciation files break NMVOCs into individual species (e.g., ethane, propane, formaldehyde, toluene, xylenes, etc.).

---

## 2. EDGAR (Emissions Database for Global Atmospheric Research)

- **Provider**: European Commission Joint Research Centre (JRC) / Netherlands Environmental Assessment Agency (PBL)
- **File format**: NetCDF-4. Older versions also distributed as text/ASCII grids. Current versions (v6.1, v7.0, v8.0) are NetCDF.
- **Grid/spatial representation**: Regular lat/lon at 0.1° x 0.1° (newer versions) or 0.5° x 0.5° (older). Dimensions: `lat`, `lon`.
- **Time representation**: Annual or monthly. Time dimension `time`. Annual files contain one timestep per year. Monthly files have 12 timesteps. Coverage from 1970 to ~2–3 years prior to release.
- **Variable naming conventions**: Typically the variable is named `emi_{species}` or simply the species name (e.g., `NOx`, `SO2`, `CO`). Filenames encode sector and species, e.g., `v8.0_FT2022_GHG_CO2_excl_short-cycle_org_C_2022_TOTALS.0.1x0.1.nc`.
- **Units**: `kg m-2 s-1` in processed versions for models. Raw EDGAR data often in `kg/m2/s` or `ton/year/cell` depending on product.
- **Sector breakdown**: IPCC 1996/2006 sector codes (e.g., `1A1` for energy industries, `1A3b` for road transport). Distributed as separate files per sector, or with a `TOTALS` aggregate file.
- **Species coverage**: CO2, CH4, N2O, SO2, NOx, CO, NMVOC, NH3, BC, OC, PM2.5, PM10, and fluorinated gases.

---

## 3. FINN (Fire INventory from NCAR)

- **Provider**: NCAR/ACOM (Christine Wiedinmyer et al.)
- **File format**: Historically CSV/text (FINN v1, v1.5). FINN v2.5 provides NetCDF-4 files and also CSV. For CAM-chem, data is regridded to NetCDF on model grids.
- **Grid/spatial representation**: Originally point-source (individual fire detections from MODIS/VIIRS with lat/lon coordinates). For model input, regridded to regular lat/lon (e.g., 1° x 1° or 0.9° x 1.25° for CAM-chem). The raw data has `LONGI`, `LATI` columns.
- **Time representation**: Daily. One record per fire per day. NetCDF files use `time` dimension with `days since` reference. Coverage: 2002–present (MODIS), 2012–present (VIIRS).
- **Variable naming conventions**: In CSV: columns like `CO`, `NO`, `SO2`, `PM25`, `OC`, `BC`, `NH3`, `NMOC`, etc. In NetCDF for CAM-chem: `bb` prefix or `fire_` prefix, e.g., `fire_CO`, `bb_CO`, or species names matching the chemical mechanism (MOZART/SAPRC).
- **Units**: Raw CSV: `kg/day` per fire pixel. NetCDF for models: `molecules/cm2/s` (for gas-phase) or `kg m-2 s-1` (for aerosols), depending on the model interface.
- **Sector breakdown**: Single sector (open biomass burning). Vegetation type information is included (grassland, tropical forest, temperate forest, boreal forest, shrubland, cropland) but typically as metadata, not separate files.
- **Species coverage**: CO, CO2, NO, NO2, SO2, NH3, PM2.5, PM10, OC, BC, CH4, and speciated NMVOCs (~50+ species mapped to chemical mechanisms like MOZART-T1, SAPRC99, GEOS-Chem).

---

## 4. GFED (Global Fire Emissions Database)

- **Provider**: Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam / NASA (Guido van der Werf et al.)
- **File format**: HDF5 (`.hdf5`) for the main product. NetCDF versions are also available (converted for model use). GFED4/4s is the current version.
- **Grid/spatial representation**: Regular lat/lon at 0.25° x 0.25°. Dimensions: `lat`, `lon` (720 x 1440).
- **Time representation**: Monthly base fields with daily and 3-hourly scale factors for temporal downscaling. Time: `month` within annual files, daily fractions in separate files. Coverage: 1997–present.
- **Variable naming conventions**: In HDF5: organized by groups, e.g., `/emissions/{month}/C` for carbon emissions, `/emissions/{month}/DM` for dry matter burned. - **Units**: Base product: `kg DM m-2 month-1` (dry matter burned) or `g C m-2 month-1`. After applying emission factors: `kg species m-2 s-1` for model input.
- **Sector breakdown**: 6 source types as separate fields: `SAVA` (savanna), `BORF` (boreal forest), `TEMF` (temperate forest), `DEFO` (tropical deforestation), `PEAT` (peatland), `AGRI` (agricultural waste burning). These are provided as fractional contributions.
- **Species coverage**: Via emission factor tables: CO2, CO, CH4, NMHC, H2, NOx, N2O, PM2.5, TPM, TPC, OC, BC, SO2, and individual VOC species (with chemical mechanism mappings).

---

## 5. MEGAN (Model of Emissions of Gases and Aerosols from Nature)

- **Provider**: NCAR/ACOM (Alex Guenther et al.). MEGAN is actually an emissions model, not just an inventory — it computes biogenic emissions online using meteorology and land surface data.

- **Time representation**: Emission factor maps are static (climatological). LAI inputs are monthly climatology. Online calculation produces emissions at the model timestep. Offline MEGAN output can be hourly or monthly.
- **Variable naming conventions**: Emission factor variables: `ef_{species}` or `EF_ISOP`, `EF_MBO`, `EF_MYRC`, etc. In CLM/CESM: `MEGANvoc_emis_{species}`, or mapped to mechanism species. Standard MEGAN compound classes: isoprene, monoterpenes (alpha-pinene, beta-pinene, myrcene, limonene, etc.), sesquiterpenes, methanol, ethanol, acetaldehyde, acetone, etc.
- **Units**: Emission factors: `ug m-2 hr-1` at standard conditions (30°C, 1000 umol/m2/s PAR). Computed emissions: `molecules/cm2/s` or `kg m-2 s-1` depending on the model interface.
- **Sector breakdown**: Single sector (biogenic). Sub-categories by compound class or PFT type.
- **Species coverage**: ~150 compounds. Key species: isoprene (dominant), monoterpenes (alpha-pinene, beta-pinene, limonene, myrcene, ocimene, sabinene, 3-carene, etc.), sesquiterpenes, oxygenated VOCs (methanol, ethanol, formaldehyde, acetaldehyde, formic acid, acetic acid, acetone), 2-methyl-3-buten-2-ol (MBO), and others. These are mapped to lumped mechanism species for different chemical mechanisms.

---

## 6. CAMS-GLOB-ANT (Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service Global Anthropogenic)

- **Provider**: ECMWF / Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service. Builds on EDGAR and other regional inventories.
- **File format**: NetCDF-4 (CF-compliant). Distributed via the Copernicus Atmosphere Data Store (ADS).
- **Grid/spatial representation**: Regular lat/lon at 0.1° x 0.1° global. Dimensions: `latitude`, `longitude` (note: ECMWF convention uses `latitude`/`longitude` rather than `lat`/`lon`).
- **Time representation**: Monthly. Time dimension `time`. Coverage: 2000–present (updated annually, ~2 year lag).
- **Variable naming conventions**: Species names as variable names, e.g., `co`, `nox`, `so2`, `nh3`, `nmvoc`, `bc`, `oc`, `pm2p5`, `pm10`, `ch4`, `co2`. Note lowercase convention. Files per sector.
- **Units**: `kg m-2 s-1`.
- **Sector breakdown**: Sectors distributed as separate files or with sector dimension. Sectors follow GNFR (Gridded Nomenclature for Reporting): `ene` (energy), `res` (residential), `ind` (industry), `tra` (transport), `agr` (agriculture), `shp` (shipping), `avi` (aviation), `slv` (solvents), `wst` (waste). Also CAMS-GLOB-SHIP for international shipping, CAMS-GLOB-AIR for aviation.
- **Species coverage**: CO, NOx, SO2, NH3, NMVOC (with speciation), BC, OC, PM2.5, PM10, CH4, CO2.

---

## 7. HTAP (Hemispheric Transport of Air Pollution)

- **Provider**: HTAP initiative (UNECE/WMO Task Force). HTAPv2 and HTAPv3 are the key products.
- **File format**: NetCDF-4 (CF-compliant).
- **Grid/spatial representation**: Regular lat/lon at 0.1° x 0.1° (HTAPv2/v3). Dimensions: `lat`, `lon`.
- **Time representation**: Monthly. 12 timesteps per file. HTAPv2 is a 2008 and 2010 base year. HTAPv3 extends coverage. Time dimension `time` with `days since` reference.
- **Variable naming conventions**: Variables named `{species}_em_{sector}` or `{species}_{sector}`. Example: `NOx_em_ENERGY`, `SO2_em_INDUSTRY`. Filenames encode the species.
- **Units**: `kg m-2 s-1`.
- **Sector breakdown**: Sectors as separate variables or files: `AIR` (aircraft), `SHIPS`, `ENERGY`, `INDUSTRY`, `TRANSPORT`, `RESIDENTIAL`, `AGRICULTURE`, `WASTE`, plus natural/biomass burning sources in some configurations.
- **Species coverage**: SO2, NOx, CO, NMVOC, NH3, BC, OC, PM2.5, PM10, CH4. VOC speciation tables available.

---

## 8. GOCART-2G (relevant to MUSICA/MusicBox)

- **Provider**: NASA GMAO (Arlindo da Silva et al.), used in GEOS/GEOS-Chem and being integrated into MUSICA.
- **File format**: NetCDF-4 (COARDS/CF compliant). Historically also in GEOS binary format (now deprecated).
- **Grid/spatial representation**: Regular lat/lon at various resolutions (2° x 2.5°, 1° x 1.25°, 0.5° x 0.625° matching GEOS grids). Can also operate on cubed-sphere grids in GEOS. Dimensions: `lat`, `lon`, `lev` (for 3D sources like aviation).

- **Variable naming conventions**: Species-specific variables with GOCART naming, e.g., `DU` (dust, with size bins `DU001`–`DU005`), `SS` (sea salt), `SO2`, `SO4`, `BC`, `OC`, `DMS`, `CO`. Biomass burning variables: `biomass_{species}`. Emission variables use `EMI` prefix in some configurations.

- **Sector breakdown**: Separate files for different source types: anthropogenic, biomass burning (QFED, GFED), biogenic, dust, sea salt, volcanic (continuous degassing and eruptive). The 2G (second generation) version reorganizes around a component-based architecture.
- **Species coverage**: Primarily aerosol-focused: dust (5 size bins), sea salt (5 size bins), sulfate (SO2, SO4, DMS, MSA), carbonaceous (BC, OC, brown carbon in 2G), CO. Coupling to full chemistry via GEOS-Chem.

---

## Summary Table of Key Format Properties

| Inventory | Format | Resolution | Time | Units | Sector Method |
|-----------|--------|-----------|------|-------|--------------|
| CEDS | NC4 | 0.5° | Monthly | kg/m2/s | Separate variables |
| EDGAR | NC4/HDF5 | 0.1° | Annual/Monthly | kg/m2/s | Separate files |
| FINN | CSV/NC4 | Point/regridded | Daily | kg/day or molec/cm2/s | Single (fire) |
| GFED | HDF5/NC4 | 0.25° | Monthly+daily scaling | kg DM/m2/month | 6 fire types |
| MEGAN | NC4 (inputs) | 0.5° (inputs) | Online/climatology | ug/m2/hr (EFs) | Single (biogenic) |
| CAMS-GLOB | NC4 | 0.1° | Monthly | kg/m2/s | Separate files |
| HTAP | NC4 | 0.1° | Monthly | kg/m2/s | Separate vars/files |
| GOCART-2G | NC4 | Various | Monthly/daily | kg/m2/s | Separate files |

## Key Design Implications for MIEM

1. **NetCDF is universal**: Every major inventory uses NetCDF-4 (or HDF5 which NetCDF-4 reads). The NetCDF-C API is the right choice.

2. **Units are mostly standardized**: `kg m-2 s-1` is the dominant unit for model-ready data. MIEM should expect this as the default and support conversion from common alternatives (`molecules/cm2/s`, `kg/day`, `kg/grid-cell/month`).
